name: Debrand: find every place a forbidden name shows, replace it where a write exists and report the rest

mcpOnly.reason: The scans read and the replacements write with MCP tools; the places no tool may write are reported, not skipped.

hosted.reason: Nothing here needs SQL or a recycle.

steps.title: Look up the website and its settings item
steps.trap: A lookup: the website must exist.

steps.title: Every page and paragraph text of the website: page titles, meta titles, headers and footers, item and nested item fields
steps.trap: apply_translation writes the unit onto the page it names, so on the master language it is an in-place text write. Every place goes in one call (batch): written one call per unit, a paragraph Header write after a separate write of the page title answered success and read back unchanged. A page Title rewrites the menu text and, with no pinned url name, the page's address.

steps.title: The website settings texts: site name, social and meta fields of the Swift-v2_Master item
steps.trap: The storefront serves the website settings from its cache until the host recycles.

scan.unwritable: renaming a website breaks the serializer manifests whose file paths key off its name; the website settings' MetaSiteName carries the brand instead

steps.title: The names of the shops and channels

scan.unwritable: a shop rename is reported for a person to make in the shop settings; no shop write is measured for this recipe

probes.title: No forbidden name in a rendered page's title
No forbidden name in a rendered page's h1 headings
No forbidden name in the mail templates

bindings.reason: read_file reads one template at a time and is not a list or get tool on the read allowlist; the order and notification mail templates under /Files/Templates are checked by hand until a scan over a template folder is allowlisted

provenOn.evidence: a fictional forbidden name planted in a page's meta title, title, a paragraph header and title, a body text, a footer-like copyright paragraph and the website's MetaSiteName; content.page-seo.1-verify.json listed all seven places (4 of 12), content.page-seo.2-apply.json replaced them in one batched call and read each back (12 of 12), content.page-seo.3-verify.json, content.page-seo.4-apply-again.json and content.page-seo.5-mcponly-apply.json (7 of 7, nothing written); the rendered page and the home page then carried the name zero times

traps: The forbidden names come from the input only; a recipe or test never carries a real name.
The scan matches ignoring case and replaces every occurrence in the field with the replacement as written, so a forbidden 'Fabrikam' also rewrites 'FABRIKAM'.
The scans read stored text: HTML entities stay encoded, so a forbidden name with '&' is written as '&' to match a rich-text field.

A rendered page carries text no scan reads (a product name, a template literal, a translation key): the rendered probes cover the page title and h1 only, and a browser check of the whole page remains.
